description:
WebsitePublisher.ai — Build and publish websites through AI conversation
WebsitePublisher.ai is a remote MCP server that gives AI assistants the power to create, manage and publish complete websites. No local installation required — connect via OAuth 2.1 and start building.
27 tools across 5 API domains:

Pages — Create, edit and publish HTML pages with full asset management
Assets — Upload images, CSS, JavaScript and other files
Entities & Records — Structured data storage for dynamic content
Integrations — Connect external services like Stripe, Mailgun, SendGrid
Project Management — Create projects, manage settings, custom domains

Key features:

Remote server — nothing to install
OAuth 2.1 with auto-discovery (RFC 9728)
Streamable HTTP transport
Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Mistral/Le Chat, Cursor and more
Free tier available, paid plans from €9/month

Get started: Connect your AI assistant to https://mcp.websitepublisher.ai/ — OAuth handles the rest automatically.
📖 Docs: https://w

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all projects the authenticated user has access to

tools.name: get_project_status
tools.description: Get detailed status of a specific project including page, asset, and entity counts

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: List all pages in a project

tools.name: get_page
tools.description: Get a specific page with its content. Returns version and version_hash for use with patch_page.

tools.name: create_page
tools.description: Create a new page with HTML content

tools.name: update_page
tools.description: Replace an existing page with full new content. For small changes, use patch_page instead — it saves tokens and preserves version history.

tools.name: delete_page
tools.description: Delete a page

tools.name: patch_page
tools.description: Apply targeted changes to an existing page without sending the full content. Requires base_version_hash from get_page to prevent conflicts. Supports replace and delete operations. Much more efficient than update_page for small edits.

find.description: Exact string to find in the page content (must match exactly once)

patches.description: Array of patch operations. Each patch needs: operation ("replace" or "delete"), find (exact string to locate). For replace: also include replace (new string). The find string must match exactly once in the page content.

patch_summary.description: Brief description of what was changed (optional, stored in version history)

base_version_hash.description: The version_hash from get_page response. Ensures no conflicting changes.

tools.name: get_page_versions
tools.description: Get the version history of a page. Returns metadata (version numbers, hashes, timestamps, change summaries) — no content. Useful to check what changed or find a version to rollback to.

tools.name: rollback_page
tools.description: Rollback a page to a previous version. Creates a new version with the old content (audit trail preserved). Specify either target_version (number) or target_version_hash. Use get_page_versions to find available versions.

target_version.description: Version number to rollback to (use this OR target_version_hash)

target_version_hash.description: Version hash to rollback to (use this OR target_version)

tools.name: list_assets
tools.description: List all assets (images, CSS, JS, etc.) in a project

tools.name: upload_asset
tools.description: Upload an asset (image, CSS, JS, etc.)

tools.name: delete_asset
tools.description: Delete an asset

tools.name: list_entities
tools.description: List all entities (data models) in a project. Entities are like database tables that store structured data.

tools.name: create_entity
tools.description: Create a new entity (data model). Example: create a "blogpost" entity with title, content, author fields.

plural.description: Plural form of entity name (optional, defaults to name + "s")

properties.description: Array of property definitions. Each property needs: name (string), type (varchar|text|int|datetime|tinyint), length (optional), required (optional boolean)

public_read.description: Enable public read-only access without authentication (optional, default: false). When true, records are accessible via /mapi/public/{projectId}/{entity}.

tools.name: get_entity_schema
tools.description: Get the schema definition of an entity, including all its properties and their types

tools.name: delete_entity
tools.description: Delete an entity and ALL its data. This action cannot be undone!

tools.name: update_entity
tools.description: Update entity metadata such as plural name, description, or public_read access. Set public_read to true to make entity data accessible without authentication via /mapi/public/{projectId}/{entity}.

public_read.description: Enable/disable public read-only access without authentication (optional, default: false)

tools.name: list_records
tools.description: List all records of an entity type with optional pagination

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: Get a single record by ID

tools.name: create_record
tools.description: Create a new record in an entity. Fields depend on the entity schema.

data.description: Record data as key-value pairs matching the entity schema

tools.name: update_record
tools.description: Update an existing record. Only provided fields will be updated.

data.description: Fields to update as key-value pairs

tools.name: delete_record
tools.description: Delete a record by ID

tools.name: vault_list_secrets
tools.description: List all secrets stored in a project's vault. Returns metadata only (key names, prefixes, service types, status) — never the actual secret values. Use this to check what credentials are stored before setting up integrations.

tools.name: vault_store_secret
tools.description: Store or update a secret in the project vault. The value is encrypted with AES-256-GCM and can never be read back. Use this to save API keys for integrations. If the key_name already exists, the value is replaced. For integration setup, prefer setup_integration which handles validation.

value.description: The secret value to encrypt and store (e.g., the actual API key)

key_name.description: Unique identifier for the secret (lowercase, underscores, e.g., "resend_api_key", "mollie_api_key")

description.description: Human-readable description (e.g., "Resend API key for transactional email") — optional

tools.name: vault_delete_secret
tools.description: Permanently delete a secret from the project vault. This cannot be undone. The encrypted value is destroyed.

key_name.description: The secret key name to delete (e.g., "resend_api_key")

tools.name: list_integrations
tools.description: List all available integrations and their configuration status for a project. Shows which integrations are fully configured (vault secrets present and ready to use) and which are available but need setup. Each integration includes its available endpoints.

tools.name: setup_integration
tools.description: Configure an integration by storing its required API keys in the vault. Validates key format against the integration manifest. After setup, the integration endpoints become available for execute_integration calls. Use list_integrations first to see what secrets are required.

secrets.description: Key-value pairs of secret names and their values. Example for Resend: {"resend_api_key": "re_abc123..."}

tools.name: execute_integration
tools.description: Execute an integration action — e.g., send an email via Resend, create a payment via Mollie. The system resolves vault credentials server-side so you never handle API keys directly. The integration must be configured first via setup_integration. Input fields depend on the specific endpoint (use list_integrations to see available endpoints and their schemas).

input.description:
Input data for the endpoint. Fields depend on the specific endpoint schema. Example for Resend send-email: {"from": "noreply@site.com", "to": "user@example.com", "subject": "Hello", "html": "

Content

"}

tools.name: remove_integration
tools.description: Remove an integration by permanently deleting all its vault secrets. After removal, the integration endpoints will no longer work until reconfigured via setup_integration.
